theater: 平安京齋院與近江大江

battle.name: 承平天慶之亂
battle.theater: 平安京齋院與近江大江
battle.brief: 承平5年10月，藤原純友、藤原豊幹、藤原師尹聯同宮中內應夜襲齋院，焚毀院殿而走；翌年朝廷命源義率諸國兵追討，叛軍退保近江大江，一戰而潰，數月內平定。卡面埃及月牙劍並未隨軍東渡，然此役近身斬殺的實戰邏輯與青銅時代弧刃相承：陣上仍是直身雙刃的唐刀、和弓短矢，鎧甲稀少。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 承平天慶之亂發生在日本平安時代中葉，兩邊都出身朝廷，並非國與國之間的戰爭。朝廷一方以退居齋院的宇多天皇所居的內殿與宮中為旗號，實權集中在攝政藤原道長、藤原頼通兄弟與其母藤原氏所成的攝政家政，以及同樣出自藤原家的藤原時平手中。執行討伐的是藤原時平與源義：前者主持朝議、調度兵仗與官寺財貨，後者是源氏宗家、河內源氏的領袖，握有京畿最有組織的家眾武力。討伐軍由三部分組成：左右兵馬寮與六衛的宮中武官、藤原諸堂的家人與家眾、以及山城、近江、大和、河內、攝津等畿內諸國由國司、郡司徵發的地侍；兵仗則取自兵部省所藏的弓、矢、刀、馬，以及東寺等官寺出借的財貨。叛方由藤原忠實的三子藤原純友、藤原豊幹、藤原師尹主導：純友是權大僧都兼東寺長者，握有寺領與大批傭人式的武裝僧眾；豊幹與師尹官居中納言，師尹還兼頭弁，掌控內殿的日常行政與院省警衛的人事。叛方之所以能一擊得手，靠的是齋院護衛與院司之中有內應，兵馬寮的值宿也被拉攏，因此能在宮內同時放火與動手。叛軍的編制則是各堂家眾臨時湊成，沒有統一軍令，各首領各自率本部行動，失敗後也各自逃散，沒有再集結的機制。整場衝突因此是藤原一家內部支系與旁支的內鬥加上一場宮內夜襲，陣營的界線畫在藤原家內部與宮中警衛的歸屬上。
countriesEn: The Jōhei Tenkei rising took place in the middle of the Heian period in Japan, and both sides came out of the same court: it was not a war between states. The court side flew the banner of the retired emperor Udai, who lived in his quarters as the Saiin, while real authority lay with the regency household of Fujiwara no Michinaga and Fujiwara no Yorimichi, the sons of the late regent Fujiwara no Tadamichi, and with Fujiwara no Tokihira, who belonged to the same clan. The suppression was directed by Tokihira and Minamoto no Yoshii: the first handled the council, the mobilization of weapons and the money of the state temples, the second was a head of the Minamoto house and the leader of the Kawachi branch, holding the best organised private military force in the capital region. The punitive host had three elements: the court warriors of the Left and Right Corps of Guards and the six guard bureaux, the retainers and household troops of the various Fujiwara houses, and the local landholding warriors levied by provincial and district officials in the Kinai provinces of Yamashiro, Ōmi, Yamato, Kawachi and Settsu. Their arms, bows, arrows, swords and horses, came from the arsenal of the Ministry of War and from the funds lent by the great temples such as Tōji. The rebel side was led by the three sons of Tadamichi: Fujiwara no Sumitomo, Umenosuke and Moriyoshi. Sumitomo was the chief director of the Buddhist clergy and the prelate of Tōji, in charge of temple estates and a large body of armed dependants; Umenosuke and Moriyoshi held the rank of middle counsellor, and Moriyoshi was also head of the bureau of the retired emperor's court and therefore controlled the daily administration of the inner palace and the assignment of guards. The rebels were able to strike at all only because there were sympathisers among the guards of the Saiin and among the palace officials, and because watchmen of the Guards bureau had been won over; they could therefore set fire and strike at the same moment inside the palace. Their formation was a hastily assembled mob of retainers drawn from several houses, without unified orders; each leader moved with his own followers, and after the defeat each fled on his own, with no mechanism for rallying again. The whole affair was thus a family quarrel inside the Fujiwara combined with a night raid on the palace, and the line between the camps was drawn along the alignment of the Fujiwara branches and of the loyalty of the palace guard.
people: 宇多天皇是這場亂事最直接的目標。他承平三年讓位後退居齋院，與嗣位的後醍醐天皇的新朝並存於平安京內；院殿的守衛與出入禮制由院司與藤原家輪值看守，這套安排後來被證明漏洞百出。亂軍在承平五年十月夜襲齋院時，宇多避入他院而免於難，院殿卻在火中毀去。藤原時平是平亂的主導者，他是藤原忠實的弟弟，在攝政之位的繼承角力中一度執掌朝政，亂後權勢不減反升，甚至入為右大臣，但翌年在道長一系的策動下被流放。源義是這場戰爭唯一的武將主角，源氏宗家、河內源氏的領袖；他領畿內諸國之兵追討叛軍，戰至近江大江得勝，朝廷由此看見武家武力的價值，源義也成為京畿最有實力的私人軍勢頭目。可惜他在平亂後數月便病逝，享年三十八，翌年承平二年秋，藤原時平與其子源長一同被流放，攝政之位自此歸於藤原道長、藤原頼通一系。叛方三人都是藤原忠實之子：藤原純友是權大僧都兼東寺長者，事後被降僧並流放；藤原豊幹在遇赦後官至左大臣，於天慶二年病故；藤原師尹是頭弁，戰敗後負傷退往大和椀久被擒，配流越後。此外還有紀貫之，此人是藤原師尹的郎黨，也是《日本後紀》的撰者，亂後被配流佐渡，數年後方得赦還。至於藤原道長，這場亂事是他一生中最重要的一步棋，他於同年受命為攝政，亂平之後攝政實權再無對手。
peopleEn: Emperor Udai was the most immediate target of the rising. After he handed over the throne in Jōhei 3 (937) he retired to the quarters of the Saiin, existing side by side with the new court of his successor, the Later Daigo emperor, inside Heian-kyō. The guarding of his residence and the ceremonial rules of access were shared by the officers of the retired court and by the Fujiwara houses in rotation, an arrangement soon shown to be full of holes. When the rebels struck the Saiin on the night of the tenth month of Jōhei 5, Udai escaped into another residence and saved his life, but the palace of the retired emperor burned to the ground. Fujiwara no Tokihira directed the suppression. He was Tadamichi's younger brother, had held the effective government during the struggle over the succession to the regency, and after the rising was if anything more powerful than before, eventually entering the council as minister of the right, only to be exiled the following year on the initiative of the Michinaga faction. Minamoto no Yoshii was the one martial protagonist of the whole affair: a head of the Minamoto house and leader of the Kawachi line. He led the levies of the Kinai provinces in pursuit of the rebels and won at Ōe in Ōmi, and the court now saw the value of military power; Yoshii became the strongest private warlord in the capital region. Unfortunately he fell ill and died within months of the victory, at thirty-eight, and in the autumn of Jōhei 2 the following year Tokihira and Yoshii's son Nagachika were exiled, leaving the regency to the Michinaga and Yorimichi line. The three rebel leaders were all sons of Tadamichi. Sumitomo, chief director of the clergy and prelate of Tōji, was demoted to lower rank and exiled afterwards. Umenosuke was pardoned, rose to the rank of minister of the left, and died in the second year of Tenkei. Moriyoshi, head of the bureau of the retired court, was wounded, fled to Umeku in Yamato, was taken there, and was exiled to Echigo. There was also Kino Tsuneyuki, a close retainer of Moriyoshi and the compiler of the Nihon Koki, who was exiled to Sado after the rising and pardoned some years later. As for Fujiwara no Michinaga, this affair was the most important step of his life: in the same year he was appointed regent, and once the rising was over no one stood against the regency any more.
kits: 卡面這件埃及月牙劍，是公元前一千五百年前後的埃及青銅時代曲刃短劍，與承平天慶之亂的戰場相隔三千五百年以上，在那場京都宮中的夜襲裡並不存在。平安時代的兵器譜系來自東亞：九三九年的朝廷士兵手上是雙刃直身的唐刀與後出的打刀、短柄小刀，遠射靠二米長的和弓與短矢，近身則用木柄長矛與短兵；鎧甲在當時仍屬罕有，多數人只穿布袍或皮甲，頭盔只有少數武官才有，騎馬者更少，源義身邊的騎士與隨從是全場少數有馬的武力。真正決定這場戰爭的裝備其實有三樣：火、弓、刀。火是亂軍攻齋院時的攻城手段，院殿的木構建築在庭中起火，一夜之間便把宮廷的威儀燒掉；弓是朝廷軍在追擊途中壓制叛軍的主要手段，和弓張力不大但射速快，密集齊射足以在丘陵與水口把失去陣形的亂軍打散；刀則是亂軍近身格殺與朝廷軍清剿殘兵時的落點。卡面的月牙劍在這裡提供的是一個更古老的對照：它那外彎的單刃讓斬擊不必把刀拔出，是青銅時代面對無甲目標的實用答案；平安的刀雖然改成直身雙刃，靠刃口與鎬的鋒利切開血肉，邏輯並無二致，只是把同一個近身格殺的難題用更晚的工藝重新解了一遍。
kitsEn: The khopesh on the card is a curved bronze-age short sword from Egypt of around 1500 BC, more than three and a half thousand years away from the battlefield of the Jōhei Tenkei rising; it played no part in that night raid on the palace at Kyoto. The arms of the Heian period descend from East Asia. In 939 the soldiers of the court carried double-edged straight swords of the Tang type, later cutlass-like tachi and short knives, shot with two-metre yumi and short arrows, and fought at close quarters with wooden-shafted spears and other short weapons. Armour was still rare: most men fought in cloth gowns or leather, only a few officers had helmets, and mounted men were rarer still, the riders and attendants around Minamoto no Yoshii being among the very few horsemen on the field. Three kinds of equipment really decided this war: fire, the bow and the sword. Fire was the rebels' siege method against the Saiin: the wooden buildings of the residence went up in the courtyard, and in a single night the authority of the court was burned away. The bow was the main instrument of the court's army during the pursuit, the yumi not strong but quick, and massed volleys were enough to break up a rebel formation that had lost its order among the hills and at the river crossings. The sword was where close killing and the clearing of the remnants were decided. What the khopesh offers here is an older comparison: its outward curve and single edge let the blow be finished without having to pull the blade free, the practical answer of the bronze age against unarmoured opponents. The Heian sword, though straight and double-edged, cut through flesh with edge and tang alike; the logic is identical, only the same problem of close combat has been solved again with later workmanship.
tactics: 亂軍的打法是典型的宮內奇襲加戰略退卻。起事之前，他們先把齋院的護衛、院司以及左右兵馬寮的值宿拉攏，選在夜深、院門只留少數人值守的時段同時動手：一部分人直入院殿放火，一部分人封住退路控制宇多天皇的去向，藉著火光與混亂把消息壓在宮內，等朝廷聽聞時，齋院已成焦土，而亂軍主力已帶著從兵仗庫與院庫取出的弓矢刀馬退往京畿南部。朝廷方的應對分成兩步：先由攝政與內廷重臣在殿中議定討伐之策，指定藤原時平總攝政務、命源義為將，把畿內諸國的徵兵集中在京都與淀川一線；再由源義率軍在淀川水口、山道與通往大和的各驛路設阻，斷絕亂軍回到京都的路線與糧食，逼其南走。追及近江國大江時，朝廷軍在淀川東南岸的丘陵與田地間展開：弓手先以齊射覆蓋道路，騎兵衝擊擾亂人數有限的亂軍陣形，步兵隨後以長矛與刀近身纏鬥，從崩散的隊形中逐一擒住首腦。亂軍的敗因不在戰力，而在部署：沒有統一的退路計畫，各首領在合圍形成後各自逃散，反而使朝廷軍得以分頭追捕。
tacticsEn: The rebels used the classic combination of a surprise attack inside the palace followed by a strategic withdrawal. Beforehand they won over the guards of the Saiin, the officers of the retired court and the watchmen of the Left and Right Corps of Guards, and chose a moment late at night when only a few men kept the residence gate. Some rushed straight into the residence and set fire to it, others sealed the exits and controlled Udai's movements; by means of the flames and the confusion they kept the news inside the palace, and by the time the court learned of it the Saiin was already a ruin and the main body of the rebels had withdrawn southwards into the Kinai region carrying the bows, arrows, swords and horses taken from the armoury and the stores of the retired court. The court's answer had two stages. First the regent and the senior courtiers settled the plan of campaign in the palace, appointed Tokihira to direct the business of government and Yoshii to command the troops, and concentrated the levies of the Kinai provinces on the Kyoto and Yodo river line. Then Yoshii blocked the river mouths, the mountain paths and the post roads towards Yamato, cutting the rebels off from the road back to the capital and from their supplies, and forcing them south. When the pursuit reached Ōe in Ōmi the court army deployed among the hills and paddy fields on the south-eastern bank of the Yodo: archers covered the road with massed volleys, horsemen broke the limited rebel formations, and the foot followed with spear and sword, picking the leaders out one by one from the collapsing order. The rebels did not fail through weakness but through poor disposition: with no common plan of retreat, once the ring closed each leader fled on his own, and that very dispersion allowed the court army to hunt them down separately.
data: 這場戰爭留下的數字不多，能確定的首先是時間：起事在承平五年十月，按當時的舊曆折合西曆約為九三九年十一月，平定則在天慶元年即九四零年春，亂事自起至平不足半年。其次是地點與距離：主要戰場由平安京的齋院先移向大和國椀久一帶，最後定於近江國大江，位在淀川東南岸、乙訓郡一帶，即今京都府長岡京市一帶；由平安京到大江不過二十公里上下，正好是騎兵小跑與步行追擊半日的路程。兵力方面，古籍沒有留下確數，只能從編制推測：叛軍的骨幹是藤原諸堂的家人與院司內應，人數應在數百之數，多為近身可及的京都地侍與傭人；朝廷方面是源義的私兵加畿內諸國的徵發地侍，總數當在數千以上，但以弓兵與步卒為主，騎兵只是其中一小部分。傷亡與擒獲方面，史料多以「很多」「不可勝計」帶過，只能確認齋院殿全燒、藤原師尹被擒於椀久、藤原豊幹與藤原純友先後落網或被迫藏匿、從犯中被斬或流刑者數十人，紀貫之配流佐渡。兩份核心史料《日本後紀》與《日本紀略》都不是作戰方文書，數字多從朝廷的處置詔敕與僧侶聞見錄中轉述，所以精確的死傷與俘虜總數已不可考。另外可查的一個數字是源義的卒年：九四零年，時年三十八歲，平亂後數月即病逝。
dataEn: Few figures survive from this war, and the first that can be fixed is time. The rising began in the tenth month of Jōhei 5, which by the calendar then in use corresponds to about November 939, and it was suppressed in the first year of Tenkei, that is the spring of 940, so the whole affair lasted less than half a year. Next come place and distance. The main theatre moved from the Saiin in Heian-kyō to the neighbourhood of Umeku in Yamato, and finally settled at Ōe in Ōmi, on the south-eastern bank of the Yodo river in Ōtsu district, in what is now the town of Nagaokakyo in Kyoto prefecture. From Heian-kyō to Ōe is no more than about twenty kilometres, a half-day's ride or march. As for strength, the old books give no certain numbers and one can only infer from the establishment: the backbone of the rebel force was the retainers of the various Fujiwara houses together with insiders among the palace officials, so some hundreds of men, mostly Kyoto landholders and servants within reach of the capital; on the court side were Yoshii's private troops and the levies of the Kinai provinces, certainly more than a thousand in all, but archers and foot predominated and horsemen were only a small fraction. On casualties and captures the sources are vague, usually saying only that many were killed or that the number was past counting; what can be confirmed is that the residence of the retired emperor burned completely, that Moriyoshi was taken at Umeku, that Umenosuke and Sumitomo were either seized later or forced into hiding, that some dozens of followers were beheaded or sentenced to exile, and that Kino Tsuneyuki was sent to Sado. The two principal records, the Nihon Koki and the Nihon Kiroku, are not war diaries but court documents and the notes of Buddhist chroniclers, so precise figures for dead and captured cannot be recovered. One further checkable number is the year of Yoshii's death: 940, at thirty-eight, only months after the victory.
cause: 起因可以從藤原家的繼承糾葛說起。攝政藤原忠實於九三六年病故，留下尚未穩固的攝政家政；其嫡子藤原道長、弟藤原時平與其弟藤原頼通三方各有支持者，朝廷在數年裡數易權衡，最終於承平五年把攝政之位正式落在道長手中。這一安排直接碰到了三方面的利害。其一，藤原純友以權大僧都兼東寺長者的身分掌握寺院財富與大批傭人，在朝政上卻無位可容；藤原豊幹、藤原師尹官位雖高，同樣在攝政競爭中出局。三兄弟的不滿，加上旁支與主流之間歷年累積的不平，構成亂事的核心動力。其二是院政的真空：宇多天皇讓位後退居齋院，內廷警衛由藤原家與兵馬寮的人分擔，人事互相嵌套，防守反而最弱，叛方才得以在宮內動手。其三是朝廷對武家勢力的疑慮。源氏在京都近郊的武裝家眾越來越厚，藤原氏諸堂亦各自養兵，朝廷既倚之平亂，又怕其坐大，於是對亂方早有戒心卻缺乏處置的決斷，最終讓矛盾以一場夜襲的形式爆開。起事的直接導火線則是倉促：數名公卿在宮中聚議時被同黨的言論牽動，事泄之後別無退路，遂定在承平五年十月舉事。
causeEn: The origins of the affair lie in the succession struggle inside the Fujiwara house. The regent Fujiwara no Tadamichi died of illness in 936 and left behind a regency household that had not yet settled down. His eldest son Michinaga, his brother Tokihira and Michinaga's younger brother Yorimichi each had their own supporters, and for several years the court shifted its balance; in the end, in Jōhei 5, the regency was formally given to Michinaga. That decision touched interests in three directions. First, Fujiwara no Sumitomo, as chief director of the clergy and prelate of Tōji, controlled temple wealth and a large number of hired retainers, yet had no place in government; Umenosuke and Moriyoshi, though high in rank, had likewise been left out of the competition for the regency. The resentment of the three brothers, added to the accumulated grievance between the cadet line and the main line over the years, made up the driving force of the rising. Second, there was a vacuum in the governance of the retired court: after Udai handed over the throne and retired to the Saiin, the inner palace guard was shared between the Fujiwara and the Guards bureau, the two personnel systems interlocked so closely that the defence was weakest of all, which is how the rebels were able to act inside the palace. Third, the court distrusted the military houses. The armed retainers of the Minamoto around Kyoto grew ever thicker, and the various Fujiwara houses each kept troops of their own; the court relied on such men to put down disorder while fearing that they would grow too strong, and it had long been wary of the rebels without resolving them, so that the accumulated grievance finally broke out in the form of a night raid. The immediate spark was haste: during a council in the palace several courtiers were carried away by what their own party was saying, and once the matter was known there was no way back, so the rising was fixed for the tenth month of Jōhei 5.
impact: 平亂的直接後果，是藤原氏內部的權力版圖徹底重畫。源義以最小的代價贏得朝廷的倚重，成為京畿最具號召力的武家首腦，藤原時平也借此鞏固了攝政實權。然而這份功勞只維持了不到一年：九四零年源義病逝，源氏在朝中頓失武力支柱；同年秋天，道長一系策動承平之政變，藤原時平與源義之子源長被流放，攝政之位自此獨歸道長，後來藤原頼通接任攝政、道長轉任關白，平安朝形成攝政與關白分掌的格局，一直延續到十一世紀末。藤原純友、藤原豊幹、藤原師尹三支此後在攝政的道路上全數出局，別家再無與道長一系爭位的機會。從軍政史的角度看，這場亂事還留下三個長遠影響：其一，宮內警衛的漏洞促使朝廷此後加強院門的戒嚴與兵馬寮的人事管理，內亂從此較難由宮內發動；其二，源氏平亂有功卻旋即失勢，說明武家一旦被朝廷借重又被打壓，其作用只是暫時的，這正是後來源平之爭的伏筆；其三，它讓朝廷看見私家武力可以左右皇位與政權的歸屬，此後藤原家各堂與地方豪族競相蓄養家眾，平民武裝的問題被推遲到十二世紀才總爆發。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the suppression was that the balance of power inside the Fujiwara house was redrawn. Yoshii had won the court's favour at the smallest cost and became the most influential military leader in the capital region, and Tokihira used the victory to entrench his hold on the regency. Yet that credit lasted less than a year. In 940 Yoshii died of illness and the Minamoto lost their pillar of military strength at court; in the autumn of the same year the Michinaga faction staged the Jōhei coup, Tokihira and Yoshii's son Nagachika were exiled, and the regency passed to Michinaga alone. Yorimichi later succeeded as regent and Michinaga became the chief minister of the left, and from then on the Heian court was run by a regency and a chief minister in parallel, an arrangement that lasted to the end of the eleventh century. The three lines of Sumitomo, Umenosuke and Moriyoshi were henceforth shut out of the road to the regency for good, and the cadet house had no further chance to compete with the line of Michinaga. From the point of view of military and political history the rising left three longer consequences. First, the holes in the palace guard led the court to tighten the night watch on the gates of the retired palaces and to control the assignments in the Guards bureau, so that disorder was thereafter much harder to start from inside the palace. Second, the Minamoto had earned the gratitude of the court and then lost their position almost at once, which shows that a military house borrowed by the court and then repressed serves only a temporary purpose; this is the germ of the later struggles between the Minamoto and the Taira. Third, the court had now seen that private military force could decide who held the throne and the government. From then on the various Fujiwara houses and the regional magnates competed in raising retainers, and the problem of armed commoners was deferred until the twelfth century, when it erupted in full.
result: 結果是叛軍全面失敗，而朝廷付出的代價遠比預期的小。齋院被焚、宇多天皇受驚的消息傳遍京都之後，叛軍沒有拿到攝政之位，也沒有能力另立天子或另立攝政，反而在朝廷調兵之後失去主動，退守大和椀久與近江大江一線，最終在朝廷軍追擊下崩潰。首腦的下場各不相同：藤原師尹負傷退往椀久後被擒，配流越後；藤原豊幹逃亡後被捕，配流遠國，遇赦後反而官至左大臣，於天慶二年病故；藤原純友被降僧並流放，失去東寺長者的地位，同年病故；親近師尹的紀貫之被配流佐渡，後來獲得赦還。從犯中被處斬或流放者數十人，餘黨隨即瓦解，亂事在天慶元年即九四零年完全平定，平安京此後數十年再無內戰。朝廷方的收穫則是兩重的：源義以武力奠定源氏在朝廷中的地位，藤原時平權位一度凌駕攝政之家。但真正的勝利者不在他們兩人——源義死於同年，時平翌年被流，最終承接亂局果實的是藤原道長與藤原頼通，藤原家由內部兩派對立轉為一系獨大，攝政與關白分立的政治格局自此成型。
resultEn: The rebels were completely defeated, and the court paid far less than had been expected. Once the burning of the Saiin and the alarm given to Udai had spread through Kyoto, the rebels had gained neither the regency nor the means to raise another emperor or another regent; instead they lost the initiative as soon as the court called up its levies, fell back on the line from Umeku in Yamato to Ōe in Ōmi, and finally broke up under the pursuit of the court army. The fates of the leaders differed. Moriyoshi was wounded, fled to Umeku, was taken there and exiled to Echigo. Umenosuke was captured after flight and exiled to a distant province, and after his pardon he rose to the rank of minister of the left, dying in the second year of Tenkei. Sumitomo was demoted to lower rank and exiled, losing the prelacy of Tōji, and died in the same year. Tsuneyuki, close to Moriyoshi, was sent to Sado and later pardoned. Some dozens of followers were beheaded or exiled, the rest dissolved, and the rising was completely suppressed in the first year of Tenkei, that is 940, after which Heian-kyō saw no civil war again for several decades. The court's gain was twofold: Yoshii had established the position of the Minamoto at court by force, and Tokihira's authority at one point ran ahead of that of the regency house. Yet the real victor was neither of them. Yoshii died in the same year, Tokihira was exiled the next, and it was Michinaga and Yorimichi who gathered up the fruits of the affair. The Fujiwara passed from a two-line internal rivalry to the ascendancy of a single line, and the political shape of a regency and a chief minister side by side was thereby fixed.
